__NOTOC__
'''Stephen Matthew Barr'''<ref>{{cite journal |title=Nuclear and High-Energy Physics |journal=Scientific and Technical Aerospace Reports |date=January 8, 1979 |volume=17 |issue=1 |page=392 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=iqEc00fCLioC&pg=PA392 |publisher=National Aeronautics and Space Administration}}</ref> (born November 28, 1953) is an American physicist who is a professor emeritus of physics at the [[University of Delaware]].<ref name="UDel">{{cite web|url=http://web.physics.udel.edu/about/directory/emeritus/stephen-barr|title=Stephen Barr, Professor Emeritus|publisher=University of Delaware|access-date=June 2, 2020}}</ref> A member of its Bartol Research Institute, Barr does research in theoretical particle physics and cosmology. In 2011, he was elected Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], the citation reading "for original contributions to grand unified theories, CP violation, and [[baryogenesis]]."<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://hyperphysics.phy-astr.gsu.edu/Nave-html/Faithpathh/BarrSM.html|title=Stephen M. Barr|website=hyperphysics.phy-astr.gsu.edu|access-date=2020-04-16}}</ref>

== Career ==
His notable work includes co-discovering the much studied [[flipped SU(5)]] scheme of unification, identifying the Barr–Zee diagram as an important source of electric [[dipole]] moment for [[basic particles]] such as the electron and neutron in many theories, and proposing the so-called Nelson–Barr mechanism as a solution to the [[strong CP problem]]. He is the author of the article on "Grand Unified Theories" for the ''Encyclopedia of Physics''.

Barr received his PhD in theoretical particle physics from Princeton University in 1978. Princeton awarded him the Charlotte Elizabeth Proctor Fellowship "for distinguished research." He went on to do research at the [[University of Pennsylvania]] as a post-doctoral fellow (1978–1980), the [[University of Washington]] as a research assistant professor (1980–1985), and [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] as an associate scientist (1985–1987), before joining the faculty of the University of Delaware in 1987. He was elected director of the [[Bartol Research Institute]] of the University of Delaware in 2011.

Barr, a practicing Catholic,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://stephenmbarr.weebly.com/ |title=Stephen M. Barr's Personal Website}}</ref> writes and lectures frequently on the relation of [[science and religion]]. From 2000 to 2017 he served on the Editorial Advisory Board or Advisory Council of the ecumenical religious intellectual journal ''[[First Things]]'', in which many of his articles and book reviews have appeared since 1995.<ref>{{Cite journal |url=https://www.firstthings.com/author/stephen-m-barr |title=Stephen M. Barr {{!}} Authors |journal=[[First Things]] |access-date=2016-12-09}}</ref> His writing has also appeared in ''[[Commonweal (magazine)|Commonweal]]'', ''[[National Review]]'', ''[[Modern Age (periodical)|Modern Age]]'', ''[[The Public Interest]]'', ''[[America (magazine)|America]]'', ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'', and other publications. In 2002 he gave the [[Erasmus Lecture]], sponsored by the Institute on Religion and Public Life. In 2007 he was awarded the [[Benemerenti Medal]] by [[Pope Benedict XVI]]. In 2010 he was elected a member of the Academy of Catholic Theology. He is also president of the [[Society of Catholic Scientists]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Our Leadership |url=https://www.catholicscientists.org/about/leadership |website=www.catholicscientists.org |publisher=Society of Catholic Scientists |access-date=February 22, 2020}}</ref>

== Public lectures ==
In 2002, Barr delivered the sixteenth [[Erasmus Lecture]], titled ''Retelling the Story of Science,'' sponsored by ''[[First Things]]'' magazine and the Institute on Religion and Public Life. In his lecture, Barr explored the relationship between modern science and religious faith, arguing that the supposed conflict between the two is based on misunderstandings of both scientific inquiry and theological tradition. Drawing on his background as a physicist, he proposed a more integrated account of scientific and religious knowledge that respects the integrity of both.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barr |first=Stephen |title=Retelling the Story of Science |url=https://firstthings.com/retelling-the-story-of-science/ |website=First Things |date=March 2003 }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
He is married to Kathleen Whitney Barr. They have five children.

Barr is the younger brother of [[William Barr]], the 77th and 85th Attorney General of the United States, and the son of [[Donald Barr]], an educator who served as headmaster of [[Dalton School]] and [[Hackley School]]. He graduated from [[Columbia College (New York)|Columbia College]] in 1974.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Obituaries|url=https://www.college.columbia.edu/cct_archive/may04/obituaries1.html|last=|first=|date=May 2004|website=Columbia College Today|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=May 30, 2020}}</ref>
